pr_body:
Starlark transition logic temporarily explicitly sets all input build
settings of a transition to their defaults. Since #13971, these values
are cleared after the transition. However, since then they have also
been subject to type validation, which is not only unnecessary, but
also breaks in the special case of a string build setting with
allow_multiple.

With this commit, input-only build settings are unconditionally
stripped from the post-transition BuildOptions and do not undergo
validation. This is made possible by a refactoring of
`StarlarkTransition#validate` that extracts the validation logic into a
separate function and also improves some variable names.

Fixes #14894
pr_title: Do not validate input-only settings in transitions

review_comment: Javadoc nit: can we get a blank line after this?
Not directly: It computes all settings referenced as inputs, but we need a set with all settings referenced *only* as inputs (i.e. not as outputs).
@gregestren Do you know whether this is still needed? It is the only use of the parameter `inputAndOutputSettings`.

Good question. The bug says there were instances of NPes but we haven't figured out how to reproduce them. So this at least provides a clear error message vs. an arbitrary crash.

Given that I'd keep this, even with the extra complication it adds.

Which transitions return early here? Transitions with no inputs at all that don't change their outputs? Doesn't `getRelevantStarlarkSettingsFromTransition` itemize all inputs/outputs regardless of their values? Is this conditional actually possible aside from a trivial no-op transition?

I actually think it only applies to transitions with no inputs and outputs. Actually, even before I first touched this code, I believe that the name `changedSettingToRule` was actually not fully correct: `changedSettings` further up has always been set to `getRelevantStarlarkSettingsFromTransition(transition, Settings.OUTPUTS);`, which gets *all* output settings, not just the ones that have possibly been changed. A better name would probably have been `possiblyChangedSettingToRule`.

I changed the comment to reflect my understanding of this part of the code.
Is this method pretty much a boiler plate copy of the original logic, or are there specific changes I should pay attention to?
I used an IDE function to extract it, so it should be a simple copy (apart from renaming `rule` to `buildSettingRule`).
